meta.name: Kaani, Machakos County (Kenya)
meta.description: A 6.4 km square of semi-arid hill country about 11 km east-north-east of Machakos town, Kenya (its western edge about 8 km from the town), in Lower Kaewa-Kaani ward. Tree cover is densest on the western hills and most of the cropland is in the eastern half. Stream lines derived from the terrain drain about nine tenths of the square to a single outlet on the eastern edge; in this semi-arid area they are likely seasonal, which the data cannot confirm. The village of Kaani sits in the south-west, near the Machakos-Kitui road that cuts diagonally across the square.
meta.provenance: Real-data-derived, not a survey. Elevation: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (TanDEM-X radar, acquired 2010 to 2013, except 52 pixels the producer void-filled from ASTER GDEM), resampled from 1 arc-second pixels (about 30.9 x 30.7 m) to 100 m cells (area average) in EPSG:32737. Land cover: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200, every native pixel (about 9.3 x 9.2 m, nominally 10 m) mapped to a game cover and counted in the 100 m cell that holds its centre, then a majority vote per cell; cells with at least 15% built-up pixels count as settled, and cells where open water is the most common class or at least 30% of pixels stay water. Roads: OpenStreetMap trunk/primary/secondary/tertiary roads (229 cells), plus 40 cells of OSM minor roads and 2 cells added by the pipeline to link hamlets to them. River channels come from flow accumulation on the DEM (plus 1 WorldCover water cell that drains into them), not from a river map. The protected ring along the map edge is a game rule, not a mapped reserve. Area: 37.3317° E to 37.3893° E, 1.4668° S to 1.5248° S (WGS84). WorldCover is a classification of 2021 satellite imagery and can be wrong, especially between shrubland, grassland and cropland; it does not predict anything. Soil health, soil moisture and yields in the game are model values, not satellite measurements.

disclosures: Each 100 m game cell averages about 11 Copernicus DEM pixels (about 30.9 x 30.7 m, 1 arc-second) and counts about 117 native WorldCover pixels (about 9.3 x 9.2 m, nominally 10 m). Small features such as single homesteads, narrow gullies and field edges are smoothed away.

Slopes come out gentler on the 100 m grid than in the 30 m source: the mean Horn slope is 0.13 (rise over run) on the game grid against 0.18 in the native DEM pixels, and 8% of game cells are steeper than 30% against 14% of native pixels.
ESA WorldCover 2021 is a satellite-based classification of conditions observed during 2021. It does not predict what happens after the player changes the land.

WorldCover is a classification and can be wrong, especially between shrubland, grassland and cropland. ESA's validation report gives an overall accuracy of 76.5% for Africa, and in Africa only 48.5% of validation samples mapped as shrubland were judged shrubland (grassland 70.7%, cropland 71.3%, built-up 47.1%). These are continental figures from the WorldCover v2.0 validation report, not an accuracy measured for this square.
Copernicus DEM is a surface model: tree canopy and buildings can raise the measured height slightly.
Heights are relative to the EGM2008 geoid, as published.

The elevation and the land cover come from different years: the radar scenes behind the DEM over this square were taken 2010 to 2013 (except the producer's void fills described next), the land cover in 2021. Terrain changes in between (new terraces, dams, quarries, road cuts) are not in the elevation.

52 of 43,263 Copernicus DEM pixels in the square were void-filled by the producer from ASTER GDEM instead of TanDEM-X radar (14 cells, in 2 patches in the north-west; at most 92% of one cell). ASTER GDEM is an optical stereo elevation model built from imagery taken on other dates, so heights there are not TanDEM-X measurements and do not share its dates. The producer's Filling Mask also flags 40 pixels as edited. The demFilledPct layer gives the filled share of every cell.

91 cells sat in small pits on the DEM and were raised by at most 7.06 m so every cell drains to the map edge; 6 more cells were not in a pit but were nudged up by at most 0.25 m to keep a small downhill gradient (5 cm per cell) across filled and flat ground.

River channels: 187 cells have at least 150 ha upstream on the DEM, and 1 more is a WorldCover water cell that drains into those channels. They are derived, not mapped rivers. In this semi-arid area they are likely seasonal streams, which the DEM and WorldCover cannot confirm; the game treats channels as permanent water for simplicity.
1 WorldCover water cell lies off the derived stream network (for example a pond or small dam; the data does not say which). It starts as open water but is not a river channel.

495 of 4096 cells start with a game cover different from the mapped WorldCover majority: channel cells set to water, road cells set to urban, and cells with enough built-up pixels set to urban. The observedCover layer keeps the mapped majority before these changes, and the worldCoverClass layer keeps the most common WorldCover class itself.

WorldCover shrubland (class 20) is mapped to game grassland because the game has no shrub class; it is the most common WorldCover class in 2196 cells. Pixels are mapped to game covers before the majority vote, so pixels of classes that share a game cover (here shrubland and grassland) count together. In 71 cells this changes which cover wins: they come out as grassland although their most common WorldCover class is cropland (48), tree cover (19) or built-up (4) (the observedCover layer; channel, road and settlement rules then change some of them).

A cell stays open water when WorldCover permanent water is its most common class or covers at least 30% of its pixels, even if pooled shrubland and grassland pixels outnumber it, because open water is rare here and matters to the game. 2 cells are water only because of this rule; the pooled vote alone would have made them dry land.

Housing on urban cells and their density level come from the share of built-up pixels; they are a game representation, not a building census. WorldCover's built-up class is uncertain in this kind of landscape: in Africa only 47.1% (+/- 9.7) of validation samples mapped as built-up were built-up (user's accuracy, WorldCover v2.0 validation report, Table A2.1, page 27); the rest were mostly grassland, bare ground or trees, so some settled cells may have no buildings.

The one-cell ring around the map edge (252 cells) is closed to new building by a game rule so the map has a margin; it is not a mapped protected area or reserve (no protected-area data was used). Existing OpenStreetMap roads and housing in it are kept (21 of its cells).

Road cells: 229 follow OpenStreetMap main roads, 40 follow OSM minor roads used to link hamlets to them, and 2 were added where OSM has no road (game simplification). 23 densely built cells crossed by a main road stay as housing. A 100 m road cell is far wider than the real road. Roads stop at channel cells; the game assumes a crossing there.
Soil health is not measured from satellites. The game estimates starting soil condition with its own model rules, so treat it as a teaching value.
